blocks.content: The Finance Commission is a constitutional body under Article 280, whereas NITI Aayog is an extra-constitutional body formed via an executive resolution.

rows: Constituted by the President every 5 years
Established by Cabinet Resolution on Jan 1, 2015
Functions as a policy think tank for long-term strategies
Has powers to recommend distribution of revenues
No powers to allocate funds to states

items: Finance Commission is a constitutional and quasi-judicial body (Article 280), whereas NITI Aayog is a non-statutory, non-constitutional body.
NITI Aayog has no mandate or power to allocate funds to state governments; financial transfers are recommended by the Finance Commission.
The Finance Commission submits its recommendations directly to the President of India.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Finance Commission is a constitutional body established under Article 280 of the Constitution of India.
NITI Aayog (National Institution for Transforming India) was formed via an executive resolution on January 1, 2015, replacing the Planning Commission.
The Finance Commission determines the distribution of net proceeds of taxes between the Union and the States.
NITI Aayog functions primarily as a policy think tank fostering cooperative federalism and does not possess financial allocation powers.
